h: חַג הַפֶּסַח, מַאֲמָר ל״ו Pesach — Maamar Lamed Vav

p: In the second Ten Commandments it is written
"And you shall remember that you were a slave
and Hashem your God took you out from there
with a strong hand and an outstretched arm, etc."
Why did it mention, in the mitzvah of Shabbos,
which was "with a strong hand and an outstretched arm"?
And likewise in the mitzvah of the prohibition of chametz it is written
"For with strength of hand He took out, etc.,
and no chametz shall be eaten";
and likewise with the sanctification of the firstborn it is mentioned
"With strength of hand Hashem took us out, etc.";
and in the mitzvah of tefillin it is mentioned
"So that the Torah of Hashem be in your mouth,
for with a strong hand He took you out, etc.";
and in the second section it is written
and at the beginning of Parashas Va'eira it is written
"And I will redeem you with an outstretched arm
and in the section of bikkurim it is written
"And Hashem took us out of Egypt
with a strong hand and with an outstretched arm, etc."
And this verse the author of the Haggadah brings,
and expounds: "'With a strong hand' — this is the pestilence,
'Behold, the hand of Hashem is upon, etc.'
'And with an outstretched arm' — this is the sword,
וּכְבָר אָמַרְנוּ, שֶׁמַּה שֶּׁאָמַר זוֹ הַדֶּבֶר,
And we have already said that what it says, "this is the pestilence,"
does not refer to the plague of pestilence
for this did not yet bring about
rather it refers to the plague of the firstborn,
וּמַיְיתֵי לִרְאָיָה שֶׁדֶּבֶר נִקְרָא יַד ה'
and he brings proof that pestilence is called "the hand of Hashem"
from what is said regarding the plague of pestilence:
"Behold, the hand of Hashem is upon."
Only there it mentions "the hand of Hashem,"
for "the Master of mercy does not
and even in Egypt it is written
"And He gave over their cattle to the hail, etc.,"
וְאַחַר כָּךְ: וַיַּךְ כָּל בְּכוֹר וְגוֹמֵר.
and afterward: "And He struck every firstborn, etc."
And had they listened at the plague of pestilence
it would not have touched lives at all.
And this is kindness, and it is called "the hand of Hashem,"
which is "the great hand," which is kindness.
And the plague of the firstborn is called "the strong hand,"
for it was "striking Egypt and healing Israel,"
as brought in the holy Zohar
and they left the kelipos from the tenth attribute,
and entered holiness at the tenth attribute
And so the holy Arizal wrote,
that the strong hand and the outstretched arm
are the two arms of Arich Anpin,
"And with an outstretched arm — this is the sword":
הַיְינוּ גַּם כֵּן עַל מַכַּת בְּכוֹרוֹת,
this too refers to the plague of the firstborn,
and he brings it from the verse
"And he saw the angel of Hashem, etc.";
"And I will pass through the land of Egypt,"
and the author of the Haggadah expounded:
"And Hashem will pass through to strike, etc.,
and He will not allow the destroyer to enter, etc.,"
which implies there was an angel.
it is expounded as "He and His court," etc.
and this is the holy Malchus,
which is "the law of the kingdom,"
"Tzedek is known to be judgment," etc.
"And the angel of Hashem journeyed, etc.,"
it is stated: "Every mission that the King wishes
goes out from the house of the Matrona," etc.;
is the messenger of all," etc.
"He entrusted to her hand all His weapons:
וְכָל אִינּוּן מָאנִין מְגִיהֵי קְרָבָא וְכוּלֵּי.
"and all those implements of war," etc.
And this is what they said:
"'And with an outstretched arm' — this is the sword,"
through the attribute of Gevurah itself.
For sometimes Hashem, may He be blessed, reveals His light,
and as a matter of course all the holiness
and all the life within them goes out,
וְזֶהוּ וְעָבַר ה' לִנְגּוֹף אֶת מִצְרַיִם וְגוֹמֵר:
And this is "And Hashem will pass through to strike Egypt, etc.":
since Hashem, may He be blessed, revealed His holiness,
and all the life went out of the firstborn,
And about this it is said: "And I will pass through, etc.,
and I will strike every firstborn, etc.,
and as a matter of course the firstborn of Israel were sanctified,
for they are bound to the root of "Bereishis,"
And this is "with a strong hand,"
And it was also "with an outstretched arm,"
which is the sword, Gevurah itself,
which is the angel of Hashem;
and about this it is said:
And about this it is said:
"and He will not allow the destroyer to enter, etc."
And in the mitzvos of matzah, the sanctification of the firstborn, and tefillin,
it mentioned "a strong hand" and "strength of hand,"
for the essence of the sanctification of the firstborn of Israel,
and of Israel being bound to the root,
and "no chametz shall be seen with you" —
כָּל זֶה הִיא מַה שֶּׁעָבַר ה',
all this is from "Hashem passed through,"
And at the beginning, in the statement "and I will redeem,"
it mentioned that there would also be need of
"And I will redeem you with an outstretched arm
וְאַחַר כָּךְ: וְלָקַחְתִּי אֶתְכֶם לִי לְעָם,
and afterward: "And I will take you to Me for a people,"
And in the section of bikkurim,
that Israel is bound to the beginning of Thought,
with a strong hand and with an outstretched arm."
And likewise in the mitzvah of Shabbos in the first Ten Commandments,
the Exodus is not mentioned at all,
only from the side of Hashem, may He be blessed:
that it be as before the corruption,
אַךְ אַחַר הַקִּלְקוּל נִזְכַּר בַּדִּבְּרוֹת שְׁנִיּוֹת:
But after the corruption, it is mentioned in the second Ten Commandments:
"And Hashem your God took you out from there
with a strong hand and an outstretched arm" —
which are the two matters mentioned:
that the Holy One, blessed be He, revealed
שֶׁעַל יְדֵי זֶה מֵתוּ כָּל הַבְּכוֹרִים,
through which all the firstborn died,
and Israel was clarified as His portion;
which is the attribute of judgment itself,
into Shabbos from Israel's side as well.

paragraphs.text: Vayikra Rabbah 17:4 — "The Master of mercy does not strike at lives first. From whom do you learn this? From Iyov: first 'the cattle were ploughing… and Sheva fell upon them and took them'" — his possessions were struck before his children.

paragraphs.text: Zohar II 36a (Bo) — "In that very thing in which judgment was found for Egypt, mercy was found for Israel… Rabbi Chizkiyah taught: 'And Hashem will strike Egypt, striking and healing' (Yeshayahu 19:22) — striking for Egypt and healing for Israel. What is the healing? Since they had been circumcised, they needed healing."

paragraphs.text: Tikkunei Zohar, Introduction 17b (Pesach Eliyahu) — "All is to show how the world is conducted — but not that You have a known 'Tzedek,' which is judgment, nor a known 'Mishpat,' which is mercy, nor any of these attributes at all."

paragraphs.text: Zohar II 51a (Beshalach) — "Every mission the King wishes goes out from the house of the Matrona, and every mission from below to the King enters the house of the Matrona first and from there to the King. So the Matrona is the messenger of all, from above to below and from below to above."

paragraphs.text: Parallel: R. Yitzchak Isaac Epstein of Homil, Chanah Ariel, Bo 3 — “‘I go out into the midst of Egypt’: the inner light of Atzilus that fills the world is revealed even to those who do not face inward, until because of this every firstborn dies. ‘I go out into the midst of Egypt and every firstborn shall die,’ implies that the going out itself causes every firstborn to die of itself; but later it says ‘And Hashem struck every firstborn,’ implying that He actively effects the striking and the death, not that it came of itself. For ‘And Hashem’ is He and His court, the attribute of Malchus, whose action comes as a power that kills and strikes.” Connection: The Chanah Ariel reads the same two verses the same way: the firstborn die of themselves when God's light is revealed, while ‘And Hashem struck’ is the active judgment of Malchus, which Rav Tzadok identifies with the Matrona and the sword.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Va’eschanan 5 — “In the first Commandments it is written ‘Remember the Shabbos day,’ for from Israel’s side only an awakening from below is needed, to remember Shabbos with the mouth, and then the fixed and established holiness comes of itself from Hashem. Not so in the second Commandments, which were after the corruption; there it says ‘Guard the Shabbos day,’ for now guarding is already needed lest they forget Shabbos, and through the guarding they bring holiness into Shabbos. Therefore it is written ‘And you shall remember that you were a slave,’ to remember that we were sunk so deeply in the kelipah of Egypt.” Connection: The same reading of the second Commandments; it ties Israel’s share in Shabbos holiness to “shamor,” the guarding needed once forgetting entered through the yetzer.
